item.title: Numerical Data
item.description:
DataCanon stores numerical structure. The Python convenience classes provide arithmetic on that structure. This guide introduces the two interfaces in turn.

Start with a structured number

from data_canon import parse_shorthand, render_shorthand

instance = parse_shorthand("sqrt(3)")
print(instance)

The result is a Power DCI with an Integer base of 3 and direct integer exponent fields 1 and 2. sqrt(3) and power(3, 1, 2) represent equal DCIs.

A Power may have a Numerical DCI as its base: Integer, Float, Fraction, Sum, Product, Power, or Quotient. Its exponent numerator and denominator must be positive mathematical integers. They are retained independently in DCI identity.

item.title: Shorthand Preprocessing
item.description:
Overview

Shorthand preprocessing provides three conveniences for entering scientific data by hand: compact List notation, named textual substitutions, and scalar mathematical evaluation with eval(...).

Preprocessing transforms text into strict Shorthand. Parsing that text then constructs a DataCanon Instance. This guide introduces each feature separately before showing how they work together.

Start with one compact List

Ordinary Shorthand Lists use brackets and commas:

[1, 2, 3]
